deadline.quote: Admission deadline (Fall admission): December 8, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST

gre_subject.value: Page says GRE scores (it refers to "the GREs" without separating general and subject) are not required but can help if they show something your record does not
gre_subject.quote: We do not require GRE scores as part of our admissions process, but like many other items of a student’s application—transcript, letters, statement—they may provide information about you as a student that might otherwise be missed. | If you have chosen to take the GREs and feel that they demonstrate an ability that is not shown otherwise by your record, please note this in your research or personal statements.

supervisor.value: Advisor is chosen after entry: faculty present projects to first-years in a weekly seminar and students typically choose by end of March of Year 1
supervisor.quote: How are new students matched with a research advisor? | We have a weekly research seminar where faculty present their research, and potential PhD projects to 1st year students | When are students expected to have chosen a research advisor? | Typically, by the end of March in Year 1.

funding.value: "Essentially all" students get full tuition and a stipend; FAQ says first-year aid does not guarantee future aid
funding.quote: Essentially all graduate students receive full tuition support and a stipend.

also.quote: offers of admission and financial aid in the first year of study does not guarantee a future slot in any one particular field or financial aid.

entry_route.value: Admits usually hold a bachelor's in physics, astronomy or a related science plus research experience; a 3-year bachelor's is accepted; no terminal master's
entry_route.quote: Successful applicants to our program will usually have a Bachelor's degree in physics, astronomy, or a related science, as well as prior research experience.

also.quote: Is it acceptable to have obtained a bachelor’s degree in 3 years instead of 4 years? | YES.

gre_general.value: GRE not required, but scores can add information if submitted
gre_general.quote: We do not require GRE scores as part of our admissions process, but like many other items of a student’s application—transcript, letters, statement—they may provide information about you as a student that might otherwise be missed.

toefl_min.value: TOEFL iBT at least 100; IELTS 6.5-7; Duolingo not accepted by Physics
toefl_min.quote: The TOEFL scores should be computer base at least 100.

ielts_min.value: IELTS accepted; the minimum is stated as a 6.5-7 range, so aim for 7.
ielts_min.quote: We will accept IELTS scores. The minimum score would be: 6.5-7

notes: Physics FAQ still contains older wording ('GRE exams are not required for Fall 2026 admissions'); the admissions page states the current GRE policy. Duolingo is not accepted by Physics. Astronomy is part of the single Physics and Astronomy PhD graduate group (SAS graduate groups list). Fee waiver and English waiver inherit from the university record.
